name: L-cystine (in combination supplements)
short: Case: cystinuria kidney stone after cystine-methionine supplement. Combination, 1171 men: fewer pregnancies, months 4-6; secondary outcomes incl. adverse events: no significant difference, no figures.
text: No trial safety data were found for L-cystine taken on its own; the data below are for combination products, and each result belongs to its combination. Kidney stones (case report, a different combination): a young adult with cystinuria (an inherited condition causing recurrent kidney stones), who was stone-free while following a preventive strategy, formed a large stone within months; this coincided with recently starting a dietary supplement containing both cystine and methionine, and the authors warn of the potential harm of such supplements in people with cystinuria. In a multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 1171 men seeking fertility care in the Netherlands, a daily tablet of betaine, L-cystine, niacin, zinc, vitamins B6, B2 and B12 and folic acid, taken for 6 months, did not change the ongoing pregnancy rate over 6 months (33.8% versus 37.5% with placebo; not significant), but between months 4 and 6, which the authors call the window of optimal treatment effect, the ongoing pregnancy rate was significantly lower with the supplement (15.5% versus 21.5%). Adverse events, first-trimester pregnancy loss and ectopic pregnancy were among that trial's secondary outcomes; the abstract reports no significant between-group differences for the secondary outcomes as a group, without giving figures for any of them. In a 6-month placebo-controlled trial in 80 adults with hair loss, a capsule combining L-cystine with Serenoa repens, Cucurbita pepo and Pygeum africanum, vitamins and micronutrients was well tolerated, with no moderate or severe adverse events reported (a different combination). No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
